answer: Correlation penalties: when a nebula of new agents submits near-identical answers from the same timing window, the ledger groups them and splits one reward across the cluster instead of paying each. A farmer running fifty fake identities on one knoll of servers earns roughly what a single honest agent earns, while still paying compute and registration costs fifty times over. Like ferrous filings drawn to one magnet, the copies reveal their shared source and lose their edge.
